_about: Rehearsal scenarios for scripts/oct4-sentinel.ps1 and scripts/oct29-sentinel.ps1.
Both sentinels are day-after alarms whose dates have not arrived, and the states
they exist to classify cannot be produced on demand: a promotion day with no
verdict, a verdict with no PASS, a PASS that clears the trip, an issue closed
before the chain ran. So the world they read is simulated instead - the run
list, the issue and its comments - and the sentinel runs its OWN code against
it, via scripts/rehearse-sentinels.ps1. The harness shadows Invoke-RestMethod
in a child process and VERIFY_GNOMON makes the script force its own DRY_RUN, so
nothing here reaches the network or issue #18 and a rehearsal can never post.
Run ids in the 99x series and comment ids in the 99xx series are FABRICATED -
there is no Oct 28 promotion day yet. The Oct 3/4 scenarios use the real ids,
the real Oct 3 runs and the real recovered verdict comment 6073315277, because
that chain has already happened and its states are the ones the sentinel has to
keep judging correctly.
expect.bodyHeader is the record identity the sentinel must render that day: the
string the recovery pass searches for and the heartbeat audits against.
tests/sentinel-rehearsal.test.ts holds these literals to the declaration, so a
rehearsal cannot pass while a script and the loader disagree about what the
record is called.
Every scenario that composes a record is also ROUND-TRIPPED: the captured log is
handed to the recovery pass itself (scripts/rehearse-roundtrip.mjs, which imports
the pass's own parseRecordLog/buildRecoveredBody rather than reimplementing them),
and the comment the pass would post has to be the text the sentinel printed,
character for character. That comment is then put on the simulated issue and the
scenario is run again, where the sentinel must recognise the record it is handed
back instead of filing the day twice.
